title: Revealing the Gap in Human and VLM Scene Description through Counterfactual Semantic Saliency
abstract: arXiv:2605.13047v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Evaluating whether large vision-language models (VLMs) align with human perception for high-level semantic scene comprehension remains a challenge. Traditional white-box interpretability methods are inapplicable to closed-source architectures and passive metrics fail to isolate causal features. We introduce Counterfactual Semantic Saliency (CSS). This black-box, model-agnostic framework quantifies the importance of objects by measuring the semantic shift induced by their causal ablation from a scene. To evaluate AI-human semantic alignment, we tested prominent VLMs against a human psychophysics baseline comprising 16,603 valid responses across 307 complex natural scenes and 1,306 high-fidelity counterfactual variants. translated_title: 通过反事实语义显著性揭示人类与视觉语言模型场景描述的差距
translated_abstract: 评估大型视觉语言模型（VLM）在高级语义场景理解方面是否与人类感知保持一致仍然是一个挑战。传统的白盒可解释性方法不适用于闭源架构，而被动式评估指标无法分离出因果特征。我们提出了反事实语义显著性（CSS），这是一个黑盒、模型无关的框架，通过测量从场景中因果性移除某个物体所引起的语义变化来量化该物体的重要性。为了评估AI与人类之间的语义对齐程度，我们将知名的视觉语言模型与人类心理物理学基线进行了对比测试，该基线包含跨越307个复杂自然场景和1,306个高保真反事实变体的16,603条有效响应。我们的分析揭示了一种普遍存在的场景理解差距：相对于人类，模型过度依赖大型物体（尺寸偏差）、位于图像中心的物体（中心偏差）以及高显著性的物体。
tldr: 该论文提出了反事实语义显著性（CSS）这一黑盒、模型无关的评估框架，通过因果移除物体并测量语义变化来量化物体重要性，并借助大规模人类心理物理学实验基线，揭示了视觉语言模型相比人类过度依赖大物体、中心位置物体和高显著性物体的场景理解差距。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Counterfactual Semantic Saliency (CSS), a black-box, model-agnostic framework that quantifies object importance by measuring the semantic shift induced by causal object ablation, and reveals through a large-scale human psychophysics baseline a pervasive scene comprehension gap in which VLMs overrely on large, central, and high-saliency objects compared to humans.
